clue.text: Artillery in middle of sustained signal

indicators.note: something set in the middle of another word sits inside it, with that word wrapped round it

parts.note: a note that is sustained is held
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: Guns firing in the thick of a long bombardment as a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to announce or foreshadow it, a verb synonym for signalling its coming.

clue.text: Impossible exercises in pits with sulphur

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: pits are holes
PE is physical education, school exercise
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A hopeless workout down sulphurous pits.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is the school abbreviation for physical education; S is the chemical symbol for sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless situation is one with no chance of success, so as good as impossible.

clue.text: Excited over spicy letter with consideration of past events

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters get churned into a new order

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up over a racy letter, reflecting on what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospectively means looking back, in a way that reviews or applies to earlier times.

clue.text: Former illustration in book with page missing

indicators.note: something missing has been taken away, so a letter drops out

parts.note: a plate is a full-page illustration in a book
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: An old picture in a book has had its page torn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean previous or ex, as in the late chairman, an adjective sense of past holders.

clue.text: Vehicle fuel not properly guarded

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: letters not set out properly are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of this word, jumbled

explanation.surface: A car with badly stored fuel is kept under guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guarded in speech or action is cautious, which is a close adjective synonym.

clue.text: Deer united below a ridge in Colorado

indicators.note: in a down clue, below places one piece after the other
one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: CO is the postal abbreviation for Colorado
taken as written
a rib is a raised ridge, as in knitting or vaulting
U is short for united, as in Man U

explanation.surface: A deer stands beneath a ridge in the Colorado mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'below' puts united underneath, so it comes last of the inner letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large deer of Arctic tundra.

clue.text: Expressing resistance, choosing to restrict force

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: electing is choosing
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Speaking out against something, opting to limit the use of force.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside ELECTING after its first letter, behind R: R-E-F-LECTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflecting views or feelings means showing or conveying them, so it is a verb sense of expressing.

clue.text: Progressive, cross, embracing conflict with weak monarch

indicators.note: to embrace something is to hold it in your arms, so one word wraps round another

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
war is conflict
thin, as in a thin argument, is weak
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: An angry progressive monarch, too feeble to stop a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like anger; it is the verb meaning to wade across a river at a shallow point.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward-thinking means planning ahead with modern ideas, the same as progressive in outlook.

clue.text: Move awkwardly stored furniture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to walk heavily and clumsily
second meaning: in British use, old disused furniture and junk kept in storage

explanation.surface: Clumsily shifting furniture out of storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is mainly British, as in a lumber room for junk; Americans know it as timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes a heavy ungainly gait, and the noun is unwanted household articles put away.

clue.text: Expression of surprise, taken in by fraud in case

indicators.note: something taken in by another is received inside it

parts.note: a con is a fraud or swindle
'Coo!' is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A gasp of astonishment from someone duped in a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise; it splits the fraud word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is the silky protective casing a caterpillar spins around itself.

clue.text: Small cake, favourite one with number around end of buffet

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
four is a number

explanation.surface: A dainty cake picked out as a favourite from a buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' only loosely places the number beside the final letter; the pieces simply run on in order: PET-I-T-FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a tiny fancy cake or sweet biscuit served with coffee after dinner.

clue.text: Meeting in university breaking mould

indicators.note: a thing breaking into another forces its way inside it

parts.note: a form is a mould or shape
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university gathering that defies the usual mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a gathering or assembly held for open public discussion of issues.

clue.text: Combine to go round in circuit

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to pool resources is to combine them

explanation.surface: Instructions to join up and run laps of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a closed path or round, such as a circuit of track or wire.

clue.text: Delayed reaction appropriate after image

indicators.note: after tells us the piece from the word before it comes second, behind the piece from the following word

parts.note: someone's double is their image, an exact likeness
to appropriate something is to take it

explanation.surface: A slow, fitting response once a picture has been seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: A double take is a startled second look a moment after something registers, so a late response.

clue.text: Relative cheers up over first couple of nights in country

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: Greece is a country

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks

indicators.note: the first couple are the opening two letters only

parts.note: the opening pair of this word

explanation.surface: A relative raises a toast over a couple of nights abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is informal British thanks, like cheers. 'Over' just puts the turned word ahead of the night letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-niece is the daughter of your nephew or niece, a family member.

clue.text: Nun at sea? Prude, awfully old-fashioned

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, leaving the letters in a mess to sort out

parts.note: thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A nun adrift on the ocean, mocked as a terribly dated prude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like the anagram signal, but those words are part of the fodder; 'awfully' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Superannuated means outdated or too old for use, the same as describing something as antiquated.

clue.text: Look outside state's borders for conciliator

indicators.note: a word outside another surrounds it

parts.note: to look, as in look tired, is to appear

indicators.note: a word's borders are its edges, so only its first and last letters count

parts.note: the edges of this word

explanation.surface: Someone who checks a state's frontiers to find a peacemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeaser tries to pacify an opponent by giving in to demands, so one who conciliates.

clue.text: Vessel, great success, bearing north ahead of one with power and skill

indicators.note: ahead of puts the preceding pieces in front of what follows

parts.note: a craft is a boat or vessel

indicators.note: something bearing an item carries it within itself

parts.note: a smash hit is a great success
compass abbreviation
the Roman numeral for one
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A ship sails north to a triumph, led by someone powerful and skilled.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside SMASH to make SMANSH; 'ahead of' places that before I and P: CRAFT-SMANSH-I-P.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmanship is the skill and artistry shown in making things by hand.

clue.text: Shreds potatoes, consuming time

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one word swallows another

parts.note: taters is slang for potatoes
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to grate potatoes while eating up time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shreds' looks like a verb acting on the potatoes; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatters are torn rags or scraps of cloth, the same thing as shreds.

clue.text: Low revolutionary tied up

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A downcast rebel is bound and held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored boat is secured to a quay or buoy by ropes, so fastened in place.

clue.text: Difficult to grasp a variable risk

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it tight, so one word holds another

parts.note: hard means difficult
taken as written
algebra uses x, y and z for variables

explanation.surface: An uncertain factor that is hard to pin down poses a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: A and Z go inside HARD after the H: H-AZ-ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a danger or source of possible harm, a noun synonym of risk.

clue.text: Be deceitful, getting into a state, causing estrangement

indicators.note: a word getting into another goes inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to lie is to be deceitful
a state is a nation

explanation.surface: Lying your way into a country leaves you estranged from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A state' must be read as the two words together, with the lie slipped in just after the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is the state of being cut off or isolated from others, a synonym of estrangement.

clue.text: Stake in card game opponent declared

indicators.note: something declared is spoken out, so it is the pronunciation that counts

parts.note: someone anti a proposal is an opponent of it

explanation.surface: At the card table a rival announces the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the amount each player puts into the pot before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Mawkish material lacking depth

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: tweed is a woollen material
d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: Sentimental stuff with no real substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for excessively quaint or cute, close to sickly sentimental.

clue.text: Singer back in style led appeal

indicators.note: going back means reading from right to left
the letters sit within the words that follow, running across their breaks

parts.note: the run of letters at the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A singer comes back with a new look that brought her wide appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a famous English pop singer, known for hits like Hello and Someone Like You.

clue.text: Less wide ground behind energy plant

indicators.note: something ground is crushed up, so these letters are broken down and remade
behind places the jumbled letters after the next piece

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A narrower patch of land lies behind the power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy plant' reads as a power station; the plant is the definition, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white-flowered Alpine plant, famous from the song in The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Doctor sure about name linked to singular lack of moisture

parts.note: standard abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: a word placed about another goes round it, enclosing it

parts.note: 'Sure!' is an informal yes
N is the abbreviation for name
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A doctor confirms a single named case of dehydration.
explanation.walkthrough: YES goes round N, then S follows: DR-YE-N-S-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryness is the condition of having no water or dampness, a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: Church official against endless remorse in retirement

parts.note: v is short for versus, against

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
with no end, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: regret is remorse

explanation.surface: A church officer, now retired, refuses to be eaten up by regret.
explanation.walkthrough: REGRET loses its last letter, then the remainder turns round behind V.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger is a caretaker and attendant in a church who looks after the building and leads processions.
